Floor markings on a gentle watch
New handlers should know why

This page covers the floor markings and lane discipline that keep the Companion Animal Travel Desk moving without panic. The markings are not decoration. They guide people, carriers, and animal teams away from crowding, sudden stops, and unsafe crossings. If you step outside them, you slow checks and raise stress for every animal in care.

Use the lines to separate intake, review, and handoff work. Keep your body turned to the animal side when possible, speak softly, and move with purpose. A calm handler lowers tension faster than force ever will. If a pet is restless, pause and reset your position rather than pressing forward. The safest path is the one you can hold steady.

The safety coordinator watches for blocked lanes, loose items, wet floors, and sharp edges. Report any hazard at once and do not wait for someone else to notice it. The passenger coordinator will guide the required travel steps and may direct you to hold a traveler, redirect a family member, or return to the marked route. <<FACT F092>> Follow the marked path even when the area feels quiet, because quiet can change fast when an animal startles or a carrier shifts.

Give special care to species, temperament, and comfort. Some animals settle when the handler speaks first and moves later. Others need extra distance, a slower approach, or a brief stop before the next handoff. Never cut across a marked zone to save effort. Never place a carrier on an unmarked surface if a clear lane is open. Keep your hands free, your eyes forward, and your attention on the next safe step.

Remember that the markings protect the animal, the traveler, and your crew, so use them without hesitation.
